title: Converters with a generic method per constant

blocks.text: `enum DataConverter<T>` is illegal, but a method of an enum may declare its own type parameter: `<T> T convert(Object input, Class<T> targetType)`. The type is chosen at each call, so one constant serves `Integer`, `Long` and `Double` callers alike. The page's pitfall is `return (T) obj;`: erasure makes that cast do nothing, so a wrong type surfaces later, elsewhere. Casting with the `Class<T>` token fails at once.
Fill in each constant's `convert`, and write `safeConvert`:

items: `STRING_TO_NUMBER`: parse `String.valueOf(input)` as the target type, one of `Integer`, `Long`, `Double` or `Float`. Any other target throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.
`IDENTITY`: `input` itself, checked with `targetType`: a value of another type throws `ClassCastException` inside `convert`.
`<T> Optional<T> safeConvert(Object input, Class<T> targetType)`: the conversion, or an empty `Optional` if the conversion fails for any reason.

cases.says: Each constant converts its input to the type the caller asks for, resolved at the call site.
IDENTITY.convert("hello", Integer.class) throws ClassCastException inside convert(), even when the caller ignores the result.
STRING_TO_NUMBER converts "10000000000" to a Long, parsing it as a long.
A target the constant does not support is refused with UnsupportedOperationException, instead of returning null: Boolean for STRING_TO_NUMBER, anything but String (even Object) for TO_STRING.
safeConvert() gives an empty Optional for every kind of failure: text that does not parse, an unsupported target, or a value of the wrong type.

origin.section: Q1: Why can't Java enums have type parameters, and how do generic methods work around this?

concepts: A Class<T> parameter lets a generic enum method cast with Class.cast, which fails at once, instead of an unchecked (T) cast that fails later.
An enum cannot be generic, but its methods, abstract ones included, can declare their own type parameters and be overridden per constant.
A safe conversion method returns Optional<T> instead of throwing.
